upstream_integration.tests: Both SDKs rerun the five new runtime-varargs, fixed prefix and LLVM frame-pointee regressions.

paging_baseline.scope: The just-completed full 848-case paging suite per SDK has 846 passes and two LA57 hardware skips. Its lower instruction, paging/control, debug and event owners are unchanged here. The complete paged generated-source/execution suite is rebuilt and rerun after this change and upstream integration.

artifacts.retention: Generated C and manifests use unique fixture labels and are retained. Successful shared libraries are disposable and removed by the existing fixture.

totals.deduplication: Focused red/green and prior paging cases are not added to this primary total; alternate-core and upstream integration replays are separate.

review: Independent read-only review identified and verified fixes for Tasks admission and a malformed segment-limit test fixture, then confirmed moving pending-state authentication before halt/shutdown/budget exits. The executed regressions cover changed GPR/control/stop flags with zero budget, followed by successful repair/resume. Static review reported no remaining blocker within this scope.
boundaries: External arrival timing, APIC/PIC/CR8 priority arbitration, SMI/INIT/RESET/machine-check production are outside this explicitly selected input API.

KVM original streams initialize SREGS once, execute actual mode-changing instructions to STI/HLT and then accept injected IRQ/NMI. Real IRETQ handlers unblock a second NMI without host mode or blocker rewrites. This is KVM-mediated execution evidence, not bare-metal microcode qualification.

Native wake/IRET comparisons check defined GPR low halves, CS/SS caches, descriptor-table/TR coordinates, controls, NMI/shadow state and complete ordinary RAM; undefined non64 high/extended banks use supplied witnesses rather than matching arbitrary host choices.

This is an internal C++ embedding boundary. It adds no stable SDK layout or general mixed-mode C export and no NeverC 32-bit source target. Generated source remains host x64; Clang owns the separate upstream i386 source regressions.
Other non64 state-owner integrations, real/unreal execution, software SMM/SGX and unbound event producers remain global gaps.
The supplied GitHub Actions runners had no usable SGX1/EPC/device and executed zero enclave instructions; this checkpoint adds no physical SGX evidence.
No final LLVM release is declared. Production pin neverd-llvm-v23.0.0-r6 and the LLVM gitlink remain unchanged.
